'''Welsh cakes''' (Welsh: ''picau ar y maen'') are a popular cake in Wales that are similar to [[Cookbook:Scone|scones]] and Cornish Heavy cakes.

==Ingredients==
* 450 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] or 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]]) plain [[Cookbook:flour|flour]]
* 225 g (1 cup or 8 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:butter|butter]]
* 170 g (¾ cup or 6 oz) [[Cookbook:castor sugar|castor sugar]]
* 4 [[Cookbook:eggs|eggs]]
* 85 g (3 oz) [[Cookbook:currant|currants]], [[Cookbook:sultana|sultanas]], [[Cookbook:raisin|raisins]] or other dried fruit
* dash of [[Cookbook:milk|milk]]
* [[Cookbook:pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]

==Equipment==
* [[Cookbook:Sieve|Sieve]]
* [[Cookbook:mixing bowl|Mixing bowl]]
* [[Cookbook:Wooden Spoon|Wooden spoon]]
* [[Cookbook:Rolling Pin|Rolling pin]]
* [[Cookbook:Cookie Cutter|Scone cutter or cookie cutter]]
* [[Cookbook:griddle|Griddle]]

==Procedure==
# In a large mixing bowl, [[Cookbook:Sift|sift]] the flour then rub together with the butter and salt until mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs.
# Mix in sugar and dried fruit.
# Add eggs one at a time, beating together until mixture forms a thick dough. If dough will not form, add a small amount of milk (i.e. a [[Cookbook:tablespoon|tablespoon]]).
# [[Cookbook:Knead|Knead]] for two to three minutes until dough becomes cohesive and slightly elastic.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll]] dough out on a flat surface.
# Cut 2–3-inch circles from the dough and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]]
# Preheat a [[Cookbook:Griddle|griddle]] on high than lower it to medium-low (this is important to stop burning)
# Griddle 2-4 minutes on each side until golden brown.
